full_judgment: 4. Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division committed error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order discharging the Rule without any independent finding on merit of the suit but merely relied upon the findings of the Court of appeal passing the judgment of reversal without adverting to the material findings and reasoning of the trial Court as to possession of the plaintiff-petitioners in the suit land with reference to the evidence on record; that upon taking needless efforts in search of title of the plaintiff-petitioner in connection with Title Suit No.17 of 1996 which is merely a suit for permanent injunction wherein the determination of dispute of possession of the contending parties in the suit land is the paramount consideration and the Court should not go into deep for deciding title of parties; that the plaintiff petitioner by collateral evidence of title at least on the date of proposition of the khatian, rent receipts in her name supported by consistent oral evidence of as many as 8 P.Ws; proved her act of possession in the suit land as against the alleged claim of the defendant respondents having no documents in their names, failed to prove their possession in the suit land. The learned Advocate further submitted that both the High Court Division and the Court of Appeal below committed error of law and arrived at wrong finding upon misconstruction and misreading of the local inspection report and the sketch map, exhibit- 10 and 10(a) which are not in contradiction with the plaintiff-petitioners claim as wrongly held by the High Court Division and the Court of Appeal; rather the said report and the map depict the actual nature and position of the suit land supporting the claim of the plaintiff Petitioner.
